transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-15 16:00 PST
Duration: 62 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Leah Brooks (CTO, CipherCore), Jon Park (Staff ML Eng), Priya Desai (Infra Lead)

Summary:
Leah: looking to validate p95 SLAs for a streaming assistant at peak fanout, decide between Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated pools vs private VPC. Primary constraints are 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for streaming up to 8 tokens/sec per session at 4k prompt lengths, and ability to support 2k concurrent streaming sessions during flash sales. Security: SOC2, customer-managed KMS, SSO.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh I'm Maya with Redwood,
[00:08] Maya: joined by Carlos our SE, we'll run through your requirements then dig into p95 and concurrency, sound good?
[00:15] Leah: yep that's the plan, we have a hard date for a pilot mid feb so trying to get scoping today
[00:22] Carlos: great, high level first — can you describe the user flow that drives these concurrency spikes?
[00:28] Jon: sure, so it's a streaming chat agent embedded in checkout, during promos we see sudden fanout when 1500-2k simultaneous users open the widget and each starts a streaming reply. average session length is 45s and we estimate 6–8 tokens/sec outbound for our model on top of a 3.5k token prompt.
[00:45] Maya: okay so sustained-ish short bursts, do you have current p95 numbers from your in-house runs?
[00:51] Jon: locally we see p95 generation latency ~420ms for 1 token on our quantized Llama 2 variant on our Triton cluster, but that's with local NVLink and lots of fine-tuned kernels; the problem scales non-linearly when concurrency rises.
[01:10] Priya: and cost is a factor — we can't burn 10x budget to meet low latency, so we need tradeoffs.
[01:18] Carlos: makes sense. rough Qs: are you tied to a private deployment due to compliance or is hosted acceptable?
[01:24] Leah: hosted would be easiest but we need guaranteed customer data separation and KMS control — so probably Dedicated or Private. SOC2 is required too.
[01:32] Carlos: Redwood Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with capacity guarantees and can integrate with CMK via network‑seg KMS fronting; Private gives you the full on‑prem or VPC control. Both can hit sub-350ms p95 for streaming with proper batching and KV cache.
[01:48] Jon: when you say KV cache, you mean prefix KV caching? like saving the prompt encoding across sessions?
[01:53] Carlos: yes, we do prefix caching for repeated system + context encodings which saves a lot of compute for long prompts. we also have continuous batching and streaming-optimized kernels that shave off tens of ms per token.
[02:05] Leah: curious about fallback — if dedicated pool saturates during a sale, can requests fallback to a cheaper model or region without user-visible regressions?
[02:14] Maya: yes, smart routing: policy-based fallback to smaller quantized variants or other regions. you can configure A/B or canary and automatic fallback thresholds. tradeoff is quality vs latency/cost.
[02:26] Jon: okay practical bench question — what token/sec benchmarks should we run to compare host vs our Triton infra?
[02:33] Carlos: we'll give you a p95 benchmarking template, but basically run: constant-concurrency streams at 500/1k/2k sessions with your prompt set, measure p50/p95/p99 for first token and steady-state token RT; also run step-burst patterns to emulate flash fanout.
[02:47] Priya: can Redwood's hosted API sustain 2k concurrent streaming sessions without dropping connections?
[02:53] Carlos: hosted can but you'd likely move to Dedicated for SLA predictability at that scale. hosted can autoscale but dedicated with reserved pools gives capacity headroom and lower jitter.
[03:02] Leah: do you have examples or case studies of similar scale?
[03:06] Maya: yes we've done something similar for a retail client — I'll share an anonymized deck. their p95 steady-state was ~280ms on a 8‑GPU dedicated pool with prefix caching and optimized batching for a 3k prompt.
[03:22] Jon: any nuance on sequence length and attention kernel choice — we saw big diffs when prompt crosses 2k->4k tokens.
[03:29] Carlos: absolutely. kernel selection and quantization path matter — longer sequences move memory patterns and KV cache benefits increase. our runtime picks kernels based on the sequence distribution; we also offer quantization profiles tuned per model.
[03:41] Jon: hmm, we use a 4-bit quantization that gives us cost wins but introduces occasional hallucination regressions. curious how Redwood Optimize ties model quality with quant decisions.
[03:52] Maya: Redwood Optimize provides recommendations and will flag quality regressions against your eval prompt sets. you can tie alerts to prompt-based regressions, so you won't accidentally roll out a quant config that reduces accuracy beyond thresholds.
[04:05] Leah: security — we need customer-managed keys and audit logs for every request and tokenization data retention policies. can you commit to that in Dedicated?
[04:14] Carlos: Dedicated supports KMS integration and audit logs; Private gives you the most control including on-prem HSMs. we can scope SOC2 controls with your compliance team.
[04:23] Priya: SSO — we use Okta SAML and need RBAC provisioning for multiple teams, can that be integrated?
[04:30] Maya: yes SSO + SCIM + RBAC are standard in our enterprise tiers.
[04:34] Jon: back to perf: what's the minimal provisioned GPU footprint to hit 350ms p95 for 2k concurrents at 8 tokens/sec? rough numbers okay.
[04:44] Carlos: rough back-of-envelope: depends on model size. for a 13B quantized model with caching you'd need approximately 12-16 A100-equivalent GPUs in a dedicated pool with continuous batching tuned — that's a ballpark. with larger models or no caching, numbers grow fast.
[05:01] Leah: hmm, our model is custom 30B distilled — might need more. can Redwood run an initial benchmark on our model?
[05:08] Maya: yes we can run an evaluation — common path is customer uploads model + prompts, we run a sizing bench in our infra (or provide commands to run on your side), then we produce a sizing recommendation and cost estimate.
[05:21] Priya: about billing: is dedicated billed by committed GPU hours, or do you do hybrid commit + burst pricing?
[05:28] Maya: Dedicated is typically commit-based with burst capacity options and overage protections; we'll include tiered pricing in the spreadsheet.
[05:35] Jon: how about cold-starts when autoscaling — do you have warm pools or predictive pre-spin?
[05:41] Carlos: yes warm pools and pre-warming policies; for streaming low-latency SLOs we recommend a small reserved warm set and autoscale rules that keep tail latency stable.
[05:50] Leah: can you explain how prefix cache TTL works and how it impacts cost?
[05:55] Carlos: TTL is configurable; longer TTL means more cache hits and fewer recomputations — lowers token cost but increases memory footprint. we suggest TTL by persona; we can demo hit-rates from our retail cases.
[06:06] Jon: do you support multiplexing single-user sessions across GPUs to maximize utilization? we do that in-house to reduce wasted tokens.
[06:12] Carlos: continuous batching and multiplexing are core — we batch across sessions while preserving streaming latencies, that is how we get efficiency without sacrificing p95.
[06:21] Leah: what will you need from us to run the bench?
[06:25] Carlos: we'll need the model artifact (or container), representative prompt set, tokenization script, and concurrency trace. Jon earlier mentioned traces — that will help generate realistic arrival patterns.
[06:36] Jon: can you share your benchmark template now?
[06:39] Carlos: i'll send the template and a sample runbook after the call; it includes load profiles, steps, and suggested metrics to capture (first-token p95, steady-state token RT, CPU/GPU utilization).
[06:51] Priya: on the compliance side, i'll loop in our security ops — we may want an NDA and to see SOC2 report and pen test summary.
[06:59] Maya: we can share SOC2 and our security packet; we'll route the NDA and SOC2 to your security contact.
[07:06] Leah: rough timeline — pilot mid-Feb, production by end of Q2 if pilot successful.
[07:12] Maya: that aligns with our typical cadence. next steps recap in the end.
[07:16] Jon: small question — for streaming, do you charge per token outbound only or also for prefix computation?
[07:23] Maya: billing is per generation token plus optional attach for KV compute; generally prefix hits reduce billed generation because fewer tokens are recomputed, but we can clarify pricing in the spreadsheet.
[07:33] Priya: also need to know retention controls — can you auto-purge logs after X days?
[07:38] Carlos: yes retention policies configurable per account.
[07:42] Maya: ok i want to map concrete milestones: Carlos will send bench template and sample runbook. Leah/Jon will upload traces and prompt set. Maya will send pricing/sizing spreadsheet + anonymized case study + SOC2 packet. then we'll schedule POC week Jan 29.
[07:57] Leah: sounds good.
[08:00] Jon: quick technical nit — when you route to fallback model, can you maintain KV cache compatibility or is there a re-encode penalty?
[08:09] Carlos: good question. cache compatibility depends on model family; fallback to a compatible variant preserves prefix cache, fallback to different architecture requires re-encoding and incurs a hit. our routing policies can prefer compatible fallbacks first.
[08:22] Priya: any thoughts on network egress for private deploy? we need to ensure traffic stays in our VPC.
[08:27] Maya: Private or VPC deploys keep inference traffic inside your network; hosted has edge proxies but we can arrange private endpoints.
[08:34] Leah: great. last thing — do you have a short checklist for pilot success criteria?
[08:39] Carlos: yes — p95 for first token < 350ms for 95% of steady-state traffic, no dropped streaming connections during a 2k concurrent step test, end-to-end retention and KMS controls in place, and cost per 1k sessions below threshold X (we'll define X with you).
[08:55] Maya: i'll include that checklist in the follow-up.
[09:00] Leah: thanks everyone, we'll follow up after we upload traces.
[09:04] Maya: thanks team, we'll action items and meet next week to confirm POC week.
[09:09] (call ends)

Post-call notes:
- Carlos flagged potential model compatibility issue for fallback; action item to test cache compatibility across quant variants.
- Customer emphasized pilot timeline — Redwood to prioritize bench template and pricing to hit decision window.
